facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Development and subdevelopment data: $j(\Sigma)$ is a Cauchy set of $(M,g,N)$ and of $(U,g|_U,N|_U)$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)5, [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)); consequently both are causal: a nonconstant closed causal segment can be repeated indefinitely to give a no-limit inextendible causal curve, which either misses the Cauchy set or meets it at infinitely many parameters, both impossible. The choice-free Cauchy side decomposition supplies every level relation $J^+(\Sigma)=\Sigma\sqcup I^+(\Sigma)$ holds ([[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]] clause (a)).

facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Causality of causal curves: a future causal curve $\nu$ whose values at two distinct parameters coincide contains a nonconstant closed future causal curve, which is excluded by [L1]; hence $\nu$ is injective, and two distinct points of $\Sigma$ are never causally related ([[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]] clause (a)). No choice principle is used in this item.

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Regularity and components: a future causal curve is locally absolutely continuous, hence continuous on its interval ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], [[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]); therefore $\gamma^{-1}[V]$ is relatively open in $I$ and each of its connected components is of the form $I\cap(\alpha,\beta)$ for some $\alpha<\beta$ in $[-\infty,+\infty]$.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Inextendibility: for a future causal curve $\delta$ on an interval $K$ in a Lorentzian manifold $W$, and for a real interval $K$ with $\sup K$ (respectively $\inf K$) finite, the curve is future-inextendible (respectively past-inextendible) exactly when it does not converge to a point of $W$ as the parameter tends to that end; at an unbounded end, it is one-sided inextendible exactly when it does not converge as the parameter tends to $+\infty$ or $-\infty$ ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d)). Convergence to a point $y\in V$ and convergence to the same point $y\in U\supseteq V$ are the same condition, since $V$ and $U$ are open subsets of the same manifold.

(Ends of a component.) Let $J=I\cap(\alpha, eta)$ be the component of [L1]. If $\alpha\in I$ then $\alpha
otin J$ and $\gamma(\alpha)
otin V$: otherwise $\gamma(\alpha)\in V$ with $V$ open would make $\gamma^{-1}[V]$ contain a relative neighbourhood of $\alpha$ in $I$, so that $J$ would extend strictly to the left of $\alpha$, contradicting that $J$ is a component. Similarly, if $ eta\in I$ then $ eta
otin J$ and $\gamma( eta)
otin V$.

(The left end.) Suppose $\alpha\in I$ (finite and in the domain). By step 1.1, $\gamma(t)\to\gamma(\alpha)\notin V$ as $t\to\alpha$ along $J$; since limits in the ambient manifold are unique, $\gamma|_J$ does not converge to any point of $V$ at its past end. Suppose instead that $\alpha=\inf I$ with $\alpha$ finite or $-\infty$, and that $\gamma|_J$ converged to some $y\in V$ as $t\to\inf I$. Then $y\in V\subseteq U$, so $\gamma$ would converge to the point $y\in U$ of its ambient manifold at its past end, contradicting the hypothesis that $\gamma$ is inextendible in $U$ by [L2]. Hence in both cases $\gamma|_J$ does not converge to a point of $V$ at its past end.

(The right end.) The same argument with $\beta$ and $\sup I$ in place of $\alpha$ and $\inf I$, and with "past" replaced by "future", shows that $\gamma|_J$ does not converge to a point of $V$ at its future end.

(Conclusion.) The restricted curve $\gamma|_J$ has image in $V$, is locally absolutely continuous, and has causal velocity almost everywhere, so it is a future causal curve of the Lorentzian manifold $V$ ([L1]); by steps 2.1 and 3.1 it converges to no point of $V$ at either end, so by [L2] it is inextendible in $V$. This is the assertion.

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Local isometries preserve the connection and geodesics: if $\psi^*(g')=g$ and $\nabla,\nabla'$ are metric-selected, then for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ on the source the pullback identity holds; consequently, if $\gamma$ is a geodesic of $N$, then $\psi\circ\gamma$ is a geodesic of $N'$ with $(\psi\circ\gamma)'(t)=d\psi_{\gamma(t)}\gamma'(t)$, and normal neighbourhoods and the exponential map satisfy $\psi(\exp_p v)=\exp_{\psi(p)}(d\psi_pv)$ whenever the left side is defined ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]], [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]], [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clauses (a) and (d)).

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Uniqueness of geodesics with given initial data: for $(q,w)\in TM$ the maximal geodesic is unique, and two geodesics with the same value and velocity at one parameter value agree on the intersection of their intervals ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a)).

steps.claim:
(The genuine pullback connection.) For an isometric immersion $\psi$ between these equal-dimensional nondegenerate manifolds, $d\psi$ is an isomorphism: its kernel is zero because $g(v,w)=g'(d\psi v,d\psi w)$ for all $w$. Thus $\psi$ is a local diffeomorphism. On each such neighborhood define $D_XY=(d\psi)^{-1}(
abla'_{\psi_*X}\psi_*Y)$. This pullback satisfies the affine-connection rules, including $D_X(fY)=X(f)Y+fD_XY$, and the local definitions agree on overlaps. Preservation of Lie brackets under a diffeomorphism gives zero torsion, and differentiating $g(Y,Z)=g'(\psi_*Y,\psi_*Z)\circ\psi$ gives metric compatibility. The unique torsion-free compatible connection is therefore $D=
abla$, by the metric-selected Levi-Civita theorem in [L1]. Hence $
abla'_{d\psi X}d\psi Y=d\psi(
abla_XY)$ locally and along curves; geodesics are mapped to geodesics with velocity $d\psi(\gamma')$. This does not treat a connection or the Koszul expression as tensorial in its second argument.

($A$ is open.) Let $q\in A$ and choose by [L3] a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $q$ on which the exponential map is a diffeomorphism from a star-shaped open domain $W_q\subseteq T_qN$ onto $C$. For $x\in C$ write $x=\exp_q(v)$ with $v\in W_q$. For $i=1,2$ the curve $t\mapsto\exp_{\psi_i(q)}(t\,d\psi_{i,q}v)$, $t\in[0,1]$, is by step 1.1 a geodesic of $N'$ equal to $\psi_i\circ(s\mapsto\exp_q(sv))$ where defined; since $d\psi_{1,q}=d\psi_{2,q}$ and $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$, the two geodesics have equal initial data, hence agree at $t=1$ by [L2], so $\psi_1(x)=\psi_2(x)$. Differentiating the identity $\psi_i\circ\exp_q=\exp_{\psi_i(q)}\circ d\psi_{i,q}$ on $W_q$, whose right side is now the same smooth map for $i=1,2$, gives $d\psi_1(x)=d\psi_2(x)$. Hence $C\subseteq A$ and $A$ is open.

facts.label: L3
facts.text: [L3] Strictly convex normal neighbourhoods: every point has arbitrarily small open coordinate balls $C$ that are normal neighbourhoods of each of their points, so that every $q\in C$ is $\exp_p(v)$ for exactly one $v\in T_pC$-radial domain, the radial geodesics vary smoothly, and $d\psi$ is recovered from $\psi\circ\exp_p=\exp_{\psi(p)}\circ d\psi_p$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] clauses (a)-(b), [[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]], [[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]]).

steps.claim: ($A$ is closed.) The maps $q\mapsto(\psi_1(q),d\psi_1(q))$ and $q\mapsto(\psi_2(q),d\psi_2(q))$ are continuous in the natural manifold topologies on $N'$ and its tangent-bundle-like target ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], [[def-continuity-real]]); hence $A$ is the preimage of the diagonal, which is closed, so $A$ is closed in $N$.

By [L4] $x$ lies in one of $I^-(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma$, $I^+(\Sigma)$; in the first two cases $x$ itself or a point of $\Sigma$ in the same component exists trivially; if $x\in I^+(\Sigma)$, choose a future timelike curve $\lambda$ in $M$ from a point of $\Sigma$ to $x$ ([L4]); by convexity of $U_1$ and of $U_2$ ([[lem-gr-subdevelopment-convexity]] clauses (a) and (c), applied to the causal curve $\lambda$ and to any subsegment with endpoints in $U_i$) $\lambda\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$, so $x$ lies in the same component of $U_1\cap U_2$ as a point of $\Sigma$; the case $x\in I^-(\Sigma)$ is the time reverse.

facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Agreement on the surface: development embeddings satisfy $\psi_1\circ j=j'=\psi_2\circ j$ and preserve the time orientation; since $j(\Sigma)$ is spacelike with a unique future unit normal, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ carry that normal to the future unit normal of $j'(\Sigma)$, so their differentials agree on $T_{j(\sigma)}M$ for every $\sigma\in\Sigma$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c), [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]], [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a)).

steps.claim: (Clause (b).) By [L5] the differentials of $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ agree on every $T_{j(\sigma)}U$, that is, at every point of $\Sigma$, which is clause (b).

(The agreement set of (c).) Let $A\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$ be the set of points at which $\psi_1=\psi_2$ and $d\psi_1=d\psi_2$; on $j(\Sigma)$ the maps have equal values by [L5] and equal differentials by clause (b), so $\Sigma\subseteq A$. The set $A$ is open in $U_1\cap U_2$ by the argument of step 2.1 applied to normal neighbourhoods contained in the open set $U_1\cap U_2$, and closed by the argument of step 1.3.

facts.label: L3
facts.text: [L3] Strictly convex normal neighbourhoods: every point has arbitrarily small open coordinate balls $C$ that are normal neighbourhoods of each of their points, so that every $q\in C$ is $\exp_p(v)$ for exactly one $v\in T_pC$-radial domain, the radial geodesics vary smoothly, and $d\psi$ is recovered from $\psi\circ\exp_p=\exp_{\psi(p)}\circ d\psi_p$ ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] clauses (a)-(b), [[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]], [[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]]).

steps.claim: ($A$ is closed.) The maps $q\mapsto(\psi_1(q),d\psi_1(q))$ and $q\mapsto(\psi_2(q),d\psi_2(q))$ are continuous in the natural manifold topologies on $N'$ and its tangent-bundle-like target ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], [[def-continuity-real]]); hence $A$ is the preimage of the diagonal, which is closed, so $A$ is closed in $N$.

steps.claim: ($A$ is open.) Let $q\in A$ and choose by [L3] a strictly convex normal neighbourhood $C$ of $q$ on which the exponential map is a diffeomorphism from a star-shaped open domain $W_q\subseteq T_qN$ onto $C$. For $x\in C$ write $x=\exp_q(v)$ with $v\in W_q$. For $i=1,2$ the curve $t\mapsto\exp_{\psi_i(q)}(t\,d\psi_{i,q}v)$, $t\in[0,1]$, is by step 1.1 a geodesic of $N'$ equal to $\psi_i\circ(s\mapsto\exp_q(sv))$ where defined; since $d\psi_{1,q}=d\psi_{2,q}$ and $\psi_1(q)=\psi_2(q)$, the two geodesics have equal initial data, hence agree at $t=1$ by [L2], so $\psi_1(x)=\psi_2(x)$. Differentiating the identity $\psi_i\circ\exp_q=\exp_{\psi_i(q)}\circ d\psi_{i,q}$ on $W_q$, whose right side is now the same smooth map for $i=1,2$, gives $d\psi_1(x)=d\psi_2(x)$. Hence $C\subseteq A$ and $A$ is open.

(The agreement set of (c).) Let $A\subseteq U_1\cap U_2$ be the set of points at which $\psi_1=\psi_2$ and $d\psi_1=d\psi_2$; on $j(\Sigma)$ the maps have equal values by [L5] and equal differentials by clause (b), so $\Sigma\subseteq A$. facts.label: L3
facts.text: [L3] Isometric immersions map geodesics to geodesics with velocity $d\varphi(\gamma')$, so the images of the maximal geodesics through $p$ and through $q=\gamma(0)$ have the same velocity data after transport by $\varphi$; the maximal geodesic of $M'$ with given initial data is unique and its restriction to any subinterval is the unique geodesic with those data ([[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] step 1.1, [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clauses (a) and (d)).

steps.claim: (Two geodesics through $q$ and through $p$.) Choose a future-directed timelike vector $u\in T_qM$. By [L1] and [L3] there is a maximal geodesic $\gamma:I_\gamma\to M$ of $M$ with $\gamma(0)=q$, $\gamma'(0)=u$, which is a timelike curve, is inextendible in $M$, and meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value $\tau_0$. Its image $\varphi\circ\gamma$ is a geodesic of $M'$ with $(\varphi\circ\gamma)(0)=z$ and velocity $d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))$; since $d\varphi_q$ is an isomorphism, define $w:=(d\varphi_p)^{-1}\bigl(d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))\bigr)\in T_pM$, a timelike vector, and let $\sigma:I_\sigma\to M$ be the maximal geodesic of $M$ with $\sigma(0)=p$, $\sigma'(0)=w$; it is timelike, inextendible in $M$, and meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value $\tau_1$.

(The two image geodesics are the same maximal geodesic of $M'$.) By [L3] both $\varphi\circ\sigma$ and $\varphi\circ\gamma$ are geodesics of $M'$; at parameter $0$ both have value $z$ and velocity $d\varphi_p(w)=d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))$. Let $\zeta:I_\zeta\to M'$ be the maximal geodesic of $M'$ with $\zeta(0)=z$, $\zeta'(0)=d\varphi_q(\gamma'(0))$ ([L3]). By uniqueness of maximal geodesics, $I_\sigma\subseteq I_\zeta$, $I_\gamma\subseteq I_\zeta$, $\varphi\circ\sigma=\zeta|_{I_\sigma}$ and $\varphi\circ\gamma=\zeta|_{I_\gamma}$.

(The initial-surface crossing parameters coincide.) By step 1.3 and [L1], $\varphi(\sigma(\tau_1))=\zeta(\tau_1)\in\Sigma'$ and $\varphi(\gamma(\tau_0))=\zeta(\tau_0)\in\Sigma'$, with $\tau_1\in I_\sigma\subseteq I_\zeta$ and $\tau_0\in I_\gamma\subseteq I_\zeta$. The geodesic $\zeta$ has timelike velocity, hence is a causal curve, and by [L3] it is inextendible in $M'$; since $\Sigma'$ is a Cauchy set of $M'$ ([L1]), the parameter set $\zeta^{-1}[\Sigma']$ has exactly one element. Hence $\tau_0=\tau_1$ and $\zeta(\tau_0)=\zeta(\tau_1)$.

(Equal points and velocities on $\Sigma$.) By step 2.1, $\varphi(\sigma(\tau_0))=\varphi(\gamma(\tau_0))$ with both arguments in $\Sigma$; since $\varphi|_\Sigma=j'\circ j^{-1}$ is injective ([L1]), $\sigma(\tau_0)=\gamma(\tau_0)=:x$. Differentiating $\varphi\circ\sigma=\zeta=\varphi\circ\gamma$ at $\tau_0$ gives $d\varphi_x(\sigma'(\tau_0))=d\varphi_x(\gamma'(\tau_0))$, and $d\varphi_x$ is injective by [L2], so $\sigma'(\tau_0)=\gamma'(\tau_0)$. Hence $\sigma$ and $\gamma$ are maximal geodesics with the same value and velocity at $\tau_0$; by uniqueness [L3] they agree on the intersection of their intervals, which contains $0$, so $p=\sigma(0)=\gamma(0)=q$.

facts.text: [L2] Metric nondegeneracy and dimension: $g_p$ and $g'_q$ are nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on four-dimensional tangent spaces; if $v\in T_pM$ satisfies $d\varphi_pv=0$ then $g_p(v,w)=g'_{\varphi(p)}(0,d\varphi_pw)=0$ for every $w\in T_pM$, so $v=0$ by nondegeneracy ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a)); consequently $d\varphi_p$ is injective, and it is an isomorphism because both tangent spaces have dimension $4$.

steps.claim: (Reduction to injectivity at two points.) Let $p,q\in M$ with $\varphi(p)=\varphi(q)=:z$. We show $p=q$. By [L2] the differential $d\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism, so $\varphi$ restricts to a diffeomorphism of some open neighbourhood $V$ of $p$ onto an open neighbourhood of $z$.

steps.claim: (Reduction to injectivity at two points.) Let $p,q\in M$ with $\varphi(p)=\varphi(q)=:z$. We show $p=q$. By [L2] the differential $d\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism, so $\varphi$ restricts to a diffeomorphism of some open neighbourhood $V$ of $p$ onto an open neighbourhood of $z$.

(Clauses (a) and (b).) Clause (a) is [L2]. For clause (b): step 3.1 shows that $\varphi$ is injective; by clause (a) and the inverse function theorem on manifolds, $\varphi$ is a local diffeomorphism, hence an open map, so $\varphi(M)$ is open in $M'$ and $\varphi:M\to\varphi(M)$ is a bijective local diffeomorphism, hence a diffeomorphism; it satisfies the remaining clauses of a development embedding by hypothesis.

facts.label: L3
facts.text: [L3] Agreement on overlaps is [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]] clause (c). Nonemptiness follows from the local complete-data uniqueness theorem for the selected fixed model: the admissible fixed coupled-model theorem [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] (including its vacuum instance), [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]], [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] or a specified independent reduction, including the tilted nonnegative dust theorem [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. steps.claim: (The union and the patched map.) Let $\{(U_\alpha,\psi_\alpha)\}_{\alpha\in A}$ be the set of all common subdevelopments, which exists by [L1] and is nonempty by [L3]. facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Two crossings in the ambient development: if a causal curve in $M$ met $\Sigma$ in two distinct parameter values, then by the segment-extension clause the compact segment between them lies on an inextendible causal curve of $M$ meeting $\Sigma$ twice, contradicting that $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy set of $M$ ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clause (c), [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c), [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

steps.claim: ($U^*$ is a development with Cauchy surface $\Sigma$.) Let $\gamma:I\to U^*$ be a future causal curve inextendible in $U^*$, choose $t_0\in I$ with $\gamma(t_0)\in U_{\alpha_0}$, and let $J$ be the connected component of $\gamma^{-1}[U_{\alpha_0}]$ containing $t_0$. By [L4] the restriction $\gamma|_J$ is inextendible in $U_{\alpha_0}$ and therefore meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value of $J\subseteq I$; hence $\gamma$ meets $\Sigma$ at least once. If it met $\Sigma$ at two distinct parameter values, then by [L5] applied in $M$ this would contradict that $\Sigma$ is a Cauchy set of $M$; hence $\gamma$ meets $\Sigma$ in exactly one parameter value, and the same holds for past causal curves by the time reverse. Thus $(U^*,g|_{U^*},N|_{U^*},j,\psi|_{U^*})$ is a development of the same data: it is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with $j(\Sigma)$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface (as $U^*$ is open in $M$), the field equations hold by [L6], the induced data are those of $j$ and $\psi$, and $\Sigma$ is Cauchy by the above.

facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Through every point there are arbitrarily short future and past timelike geodesic segments, whose squared velocity and time orientation stay constant ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]). Smooth coordinate neighborhoods give a countable neighborhood basis for taking limits ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

steps.claim: (Actual interior past at a future boundary.) Let $p\in\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and $x\in I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. The open set $I^+(x)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ contains $p$ and therefore meets $U$ at some $y$. A future timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $x$ followed by one from $x$ to $y\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ lies entirely in $U$ by [L3]; hence $x\in U$. This proves $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)\subseteq U$. Short timelike geodesic segments ending at $p$, with all earlier points sufficiently close to $p$, lie in this set by [L5] and the openness of $I^+(\Sigma)$. Thus there are actual interior past points tending to $p$. Apply the same proof in $M'$ to $\varphi(U)$ and reverse time on the past side.

(A closed past inclusion from paired witnesses.) Let $(p,p')$ be a corresponding future pair and $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$. Take a short future timelike geodesic through $p'$ and points $t'_n$ on it with $p'\ll t'_n$ and $t'_n\to p'$. For every $n$, $I^+(q)$ is an open neighborhood of $p$, and $I'^-(t'_n)$ is an open neighborhood of $p'$. Correspondence supplies $r_n\in U\cap I^+(q)$ with $\varphi(r_n)\in I'^-(t'_n)$. The timelike curve from $q$ to $r_n$ lies in $U$ by [L3], so $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r_n)\ll t'_n$. Closedness of the causal relation in $M'$ gives $\varphi(q)\le p'$. Notice that the neighborhood of $p'$ used here is the past of the strictly later point $t'_n$.

(Uniqueness.) Suppose a future boundary point $p$ corresponds to $p'_1,p'_2$. By step 1.1 both lie in the future of $\Sigma'$, and by step 3.1 their chronological pasts intersected with $\varphi(U)$ agree. Step 1.2 supplies points $y'_n\in I'^-(p'_1)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')\subseteq\varphi(U)$ on a short past geodesic, tending to $p'_1$. The past equality therefore gives $y'_n\ll p'_2$ for every $n$. Closedness of the causal relation implies $p'_1\le p'_2$. Interchanging the two points gives $p'_2\le p'_1$. Causality forces equality. For a past boundary point, apply this proof with the time orientation reversed; uniqueness holds on both sides. Together with step 4.1, this proves (c).

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Chronology is open in each point and as a relation; causal relations are transitive, and $x\ll y\le z$ implies $x\ll z$. A future timelike curve has strictly chronologically ordered values at different parameters ([[lem-gr-chronology-openness]], [[lem-gr-push-up-rule]], [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

steps.claim: (Corresponding points have the same side.) Since the initial surface is contained in the open set $U$, a boundary point $p$ is outside it and therefore lies in $I^+(\Sigma)$ or $I^-(\Sigma)$ by [L1]. A point $x\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is timelike reachable from $\Sigma$ along a curve lying in $U$ by [L3], so $\varphi(x)\in I'^+(\Sigma')$ by [L4]; likewise for the past, using time reversal and [L3]. If $p\in I^+(\Sigma)$, restrict all source neighborhoods in the correspondence definition to that open set. The corresponding point $p'$ cannot lie in $I'^-(\Sigma')$, because this is open and would give a paired witness with inconsistent sides; and it cannot lie in $\Sigma'\subseteq\varphi(U)$ because it is a boundary point of the open image. Thus $p'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. The past case is identical after time reversal.

(Actual interior past at a future boundary.) Let $p\in\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and $x\in I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. The open set $I^+(x)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ contains $p$ and therefore meets $U$ at some $y$. A future timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $x$ followed by one from $x$ to $y\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ lies entirely in $U$ by [L3]; hence $x\in U$. This proves $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)\subseteq U$. Short timelike geodesic segments ending at $p$, with all earlier points sufficiently close to $p$, lie in this set by [L5] and the openness of $I^+(\Sigma)$. Thus there are actual interior past points tending to $p$. Apply the same proof in $M'$ to $\varphi(U)$ and reverse time on the past side.

(A closed past inclusion from paired witnesses.) Let $(p,p')$ be a corresponding future pair and $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$. Take a short future timelike geodesic through $p'$ and points $t'_n$ on it with $p'\ll t'_n$ and $t'_n\to p'$. For every $n$, $I^+(q)$ is an open neighborhood of $p$, and $I'^-(t'_n)$ is an open neighborhood of $p'$. Correspondence supplies $r_n\in U\cap I^+(q)$ with $\varphi(r_n)\in I'^-(t'_n)$. The timelike curve from $q$ to $r_n$ lies in $U$ by [L3], so $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r_n)\ll t'_n$. Closedness of the causal relation in $M'$ gives $\varphi(q)\le p'$. Notice that the neighborhood of $p'$ used here is the past of the strictly later point $t'_n$.

(Strict inclusion and equality of chronological pasts.) With $q$ as above, a sufficiently late point $r$ on the interior timelike geodesic ending at $p$ from step 1.2 satisfies $q\ll r\ll p$, because $I^+(q)$ is an open neighborhood of $p$. It lies in $U$, so step 2.2 gives $\varphi(r)\le p'$, while [L3]-[L4] give $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r)$. Push-up yields $\varphi(q)\ll p'$. Hence $\varphi(I^-(p)\cap U)\subseteq I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$. Apply the same strict inclusion to the reversed common subdevelopment and the corresponding pair $(p',p)$ to obtain equality. For the second equality in (b), if $r\in I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U$, both endpoints $q,r$ lie in $U$ and their joining timelike curve lies there by [L3]; consequently $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r)\ll p'$. Conversely if $r'\in I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$, the first equality puts $r=\varphi^{-1}(r')$ in $I^-(p)\cap U$, and the joining timelike curve between $\varphi(q),r'$ lies in $\varphi(U)$ by [L3], so its inverse gives $q\ll r$. This proves both equalities.

(Limit along an interior timelike curve.) Let $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ be future timelike with limit $p$. For every $s<t<0$, $\gamma(s)\ll\gamma(t)$, and closedness applied to later values tending to $p$ gives $\gamma(t)\le p$; push-up gives $\gamma(s)\ll p$. If $p$ were to the past of $\Sigma$, then for sufficiently late $s$ the point $\gamma(s)$ would lie in $I^-(\Sigma)$, and a concatenated timelike curve from $\gamma(s)$ through $p$ to $\Sigma$ would have both endpoints in $U$, putting $p\in U$ by [L3], a contradiction. Therefore such a curve can converge only to a future boundary point. Fix an open neighborhood $V'$ of the corresponding $p'$. By [L6] choose an open causal-convex $W'$ with $p'\in W'\subseteq V'$. The interior past-geodesic construction of step 1.2 on the primed side supplies $q'\in W'\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$, with $q'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. Step 3.1 gives $q:=\varphi^{-1}(q')\in I^-(p)\cap U$. For all sufficiently late $s$, $\gamma(s)\in I^+(q)$ by chronology openness, and also $\gamma(s)\in I^-(p)$ by the first argument of this step. The second equality of (b) then gives $q'\ll\varphi(\gamma(s))\ll p'$. Concatenate the ambient timelike curves from $q'$ to this point and from it to $p'$; both endpoints $q',p'$ are in $W'$, so causal convexity places $\varphi(\gamma(s))$ in $W'\subseteq V'$. This proves $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$. Reversing time proves the corresponding limit statement for past-directed curves ending at a past boundary point.

(Uniqueness.) Suppose a future boundary point $p$ corresponds to $p'_1,p'_2$. By step 1.1 both lie in the future of $\Sigma'$, and by step 3.1 their chronological pasts intersected with $\varphi(U)$ agree. Step 1.2 supplies points $y'_n\in I'^-(p'_1)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')\subseteq\varphi(U)$ on a short past geodesic, tending to $p'_1$. The past equality therefore gives $y'_n\ll p'_2$ for every $n$. Closedness of the causal relation implies $p'_1\le p'_2$. Interchanging the two points gives $p'_2\le p'_1$. Causality forces equality. For a past boundary point, apply this proof with the time orientation reversed; uniqueness holds on both sides. Together with step 4.1, this proves (c).

For every $s<t<0$, $\gamma(s)\ll\gamma(t)$, and closedness applied to later values tending to $p$ gives $\gamma(t)\le p$; push-up gives $\gamma(s)\ll p$. If $p$ were to the past of $\Sigma$, then for sufficiently late $s$ the point $\gamma(s)$ would lie in $I^-(\Sigma)$, and a concatenated timelike curve from $\gamma(s)$ through $p$ to $\Sigma$ would have both endpoints in $U$, putting $p\in U$ by [L3], a contradiction. Therefore such a curve can converge only to a future boundary point. Fix an open neighborhood $V'$ of the corresponding $p'$. By [L6] choose an open causal-convex $W'$ with $p'\in W'\subseteq V'$. The interior past-geodesic construction of step 1.2 on the primed side supplies $q'\in W'\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$, with $q'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. Step 3.1 gives $q:=\varphi^{-1}(q')\in I^-(p)\cap U$. For all sufficiently late $s$, $\gamma(s)\in I^+(q)$ by chronology openness, and also $\gamma(s)\in I^-(p)$ by the first argument of this step. The second equality of (b) then gives $q'\ll\varphi(\gamma(s))\ll p'$. Concatenate the ambient timelike curves from $q'$ to this point and from it to $p'$; both endpoints $q',p'$ are in $W'$, so causal convexity places $\varphi(\gamma(s))$ in $W'\subseteq V'$. This proves $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$. Reversing time proves the corresponding limit statement for past-directed curves ending at a past boundary point.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Chronology is open in each point and as a relation; causal relations are transitive, and $x\ll y\le z$ implies $x\ll z$. A future timelike curve has strictly chronologically ordered values at different parameters ([[lem-gr-chronology-openness]], [[lem-gr-push-up-rule]], [[lem-gr-causal-curve-calculus]], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

steps.claim: (Corresponding points have the same side.) Since the initial surface is contained in the open set $U$, a boundary point $p$ is outside it and therefore lies in $I^+(\Sigma)$ or $I^-(\Sigma)$ by [L1]. A point $x\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is timelike reachable from $\Sigma$ along a curve lying in $U$ by [L3], so $\varphi(x)\in I'^+(\Sigma')$ by [L4]; likewise for the past, using time reversal and [L3]. If $p\in I^+(\Sigma)$, restrict all source neighborhoods in the correspondence definition to that open set. The corresponding point $p'$ cannot lie in $I'^-(\Sigma')$, because this is open and would give a paired witness with inconsistent sides; and it cannot lie in $\Sigma'\subseteq\varphi(U)$ because it is a boundary point of the open image. Thus $p'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. The past case is identical after time reversal.

(Actual interior past at a future boundary.) Let $p\in\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and $x\in I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. The open set $I^+(x)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ contains $p$ and therefore meets $U$ at some $y$. A future timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $x$ followed by one from $x$ to $y\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ lies entirely in $U$ by [L3]; hence $x\in U$. This proves $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)\subseteq U$. Short timelike geodesic segments ending at $p$, with all earlier points sufficiently close to $p$, lie in this set by [L5] and the openness of $I^+(\Sigma)$. Thus there are actual interior past points tending to $p$. Apply the same proof in $M'$ to $\varphi(U)$ and reverse time on the past side.

(A closed past inclusion from paired witnesses.) Let $(p,p')$ be a corresponding future pair and $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$. Take a short future timelike geodesic through $p'$ and points $t'_n$ on it with $p'\ll t'_n$ and $t'_n\to p'$. For every $n$, $I^+(q)$ is an open neighborhood of $p$, and $I'^-(t'_n)$ is an open neighborhood of $p'$. Correspondence supplies $r_n\in U\cap I^+(q)$ with $\varphi(r_n)\in I'^-(t'_n)$. The timelike curve from $q$ to $r_n$ lies in $U$ by [L3], so $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r_n)\ll t'_n$. Closedness of the causal relation in $M'$ gives $\varphi(q)\le p'$. Notice that the neighborhood of $p'$ used here is the past of the strictly later point $t'_n$.

(Strict inclusion and equality of chronological pasts.) With $q$ as above, a sufficiently late point $r$ on the interior timelike geodesic ending at $p$ from step 1.2 satisfies $q\ll r\ll p$, because $I^+(q)$ is an open neighborhood of $p$. It lies in $U$, so step 2.2 gives $\varphi(r)\le p'$, while [L3]-[L4] give $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r)$. Push-up yields $\varphi(q)\ll p'$. Hence $\varphi(I^-(p)\cap U)\subseteq I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$. Apply the same strict inclusion to the reversed common subdevelopment and the corresponding pair $(p',p)$ to obtain equality. For the second equality in (b), if $r\in I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U$, both endpoints $q,r$ lie in $U$ and their joining timelike curve lies there by [L3]; consequently $\varphi(q)\ll\varphi(r)\ll p'$. Conversely if $r'\in I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$, the first equality puts $r=\varphi^{-1}(r')$ in $I^-(p)\cap U$, and the joining timelike curve between $\varphi(q),r'$ lies in $\varphi(U)$ by [L3], so its inverse gives $q\ll r$. This proves both equalities.

(Limit along an interior timelike curve.) Let $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ be future timelike with limit $p$. For every $s<t<0$, $\gamma(s)\ll\gamma(t)$, and closedness applied to later values tending to $p$ gives $\gamma(t)\le p$; push-up gives $\gamma(s)\ll p$. If $p$ were to the past of $\Sigma$, then for sufficiently late $s$ the point $\gamma(s)$ would lie in $I^-(\Sigma)$, and a concatenated timelike curve from $\gamma(s)$ through $p$ to $\Sigma$ would have both endpoints in $U$, putting $p\in U$ by [L3], a contradiction. Therefore such a curve can converge only to a future boundary point. Fix an open neighborhood $V'$ of the corresponding $p'$. By [L6] choose an open causal-convex $W'$ with $p'\in W'\subseteq V'$. The interior past-geodesic construction of step 1.2 on the primed side supplies $q'\in W'\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$, with $q'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. Step 3.1 gives $q:=\varphi^{-1}(q')\in I^-(p)\cap U$. For all sufficiently late $s$, $\gamma(s)\in I^+(q)$ by chronology openness, and also $\gamma(s)\in I^-(p)$ by the first argument of this step. (Uniqueness.) Suppose a future boundary point $p$ corresponds to $p'_1,p'_2$. By step 1.1 both lie in the future of $\Sigma'$, and by step 3.1 their chronological pasts intersected with $\varphi(U)$ agree. Step 1.2 supplies points $y'_n\in I'^-(p'_1)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')\subseteq\varphi(U)$ on a short past geodesic, tending to $p'_1$. The past equality therefore gives $y'_n\ll p'_2$ for every $n$. Closedness of the causal relation implies $p'_1\le p'_2$. Interchanging the two points gives $p'_2\le p'_1$. Causality forces equality. For a past boundary point, apply this proof with the time orientation reversed; uniqueness holds on both sides. Together with step 4.1, this proves (c).

facts.label: L5

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] The initial surface $\Sigma$ is contained in $U$, every boundary point is strictly to one side of $\Sigma$, chronology is open, and every causal curve from $\Sigma$ to a future point of $U$ lies in $U$; every causal segment with both endpoints in $U$ lies in $U$ ([[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]], [[lem-gr-chronology-openness]], [[lem-gr-subdevelopment-convexity]]). The past-side assertions are the time reverse.

steps.claim: (The interior past of a future boundary point.) Let $p\in C\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. If $x\in I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$, openness of $I^+(x)$ and the fact $p\in\partial U$ give $y\in U\cap I^+(x)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Concatenate a future timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $x$ with one from $x$ to $y$. Past convexity [L1] puts that curve, hence $x$, in $U$. Therefore $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)\subseteq U$. Choose a future timelike vector at $p$ and its local geodesic $\gamma$ with $\gamma(0)=p$; for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, its segment $\gamma([-\varepsilon,0))$ lies in $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and hence in $U$. This establishes an actual affinely parametrized timelike geodesic, rather than replacing an arbitrary timelike curve by a geodesic.

(Local normal-coordinate extension.) Let $p'$ correspond to $p$. By [L3] $\varphi\circ\gamma\to p'$. Choose convex normal neighborhoods $V$ of $p$ and $V'$ of $p'$; shorten $\gamma$ so its entire segment and its image lie respectively in $V,V'$, and set $a=\gamma(-\varepsilon)$. By [L4] the image segment is an affinely parametrized geodesic. In the normal chart based at $\varphi(a)$ its inverse-exponential coordinates are its affine parameter times its initial velocity. Continuity at the limit $p'$ therefore gives $d\varphi_a(\exp_a^{-1}p)=\exp_{\varphi(a)}^{-1}p'$. Both vectors lie in the open normal-chart domains. Consequently, on a sufficiently small neighborhood $W$ of $p$, the formula $F_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a)}(d\varphi_a(\exp_a^{-1}q))$ is defined and is a diffeomorphism onto its open image. At $q=p$ the vector $\exp_a^{-1}p$ is future timelike; shrink $W\subseteq V\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ until every $\exp_a^{-1}q$ is future timelike as well. Its radial geodesic then joins $a$ to $q$ and stays in $V$. For $q\in W\cap U$, both endpoints lie in $U$, so causal convexity [L1] puts its entire radial segment in $U$. The connection-preserving property [L4] now gives $F_p(q)=\varphi(q)$. For past boundary points repeat with reversed time orientation and an interior base point $a\in I^+(p)\cap U$.

facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Under Countable Choice, $M'$ admits a smooth embedding $e:M'\to\mathbb R^9$; its embedded image has an open Euclidean tubular neighborhood $T$ and a smooth retraction $r:T\to e(M')$ with $r\circ e=e$ ([[thm-weak-whitney-proper-embedding-theorem]], [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]). The retraction is the normal-bundle projection composed with the inverse normal-addition diffeomorphism.

steps.claim: (Euclidean patching and common jets.) Use the open cover of $\Omega_0:=U\cup\bigcup W$ consisting of $U$ with map $F_0=\varphi$ and all admissible pairs $(W,F_p)$ of step 2.1. Index by all such pairs, so no arbitrary-index choice of one map per boundary point is needed. Obtain [L5] and a subordinate locally finite partition $(\rho_i)$ from [L6]; write $H=\sum_i\rho_i(e\circ F_i):\Omega_0\to\mathbb R^9$. Each term is extended by zero off its cover member; subordinate support makes the extension smooth. At $q\in A$, every term whose support meets $q$ has $F_i(q)=f(q)$, so $H(q)=e(f(q))$. Moreover fix one local extension $F$ near $q$. On the open set $U$ in each overlapping domain one has $eF_i=eF=e\varphi$. If $q\in C$, every coordinate derivative of their difference is zero at $q$ by continuity from $U$; if $q\in U$ the equality holds on a neighborhood. Local finiteness and $\sum_i\rho_i=1$ therefore show that every coordinate derivative of $H-eF$ vanishes at $q$: apply the finite Leibniz expansion to $\sum_i\rho_i(eF_i-eF)$. This proves equality of all jets at every point of $A$.

(Retraction and local invertibility.) The open set $\Omega_1:=H^{-1}(T)$ contains $A$. Define $\Phi=e^{-1}\circ r\circ H$ there. It is smooth and agrees with $f$ on $A$. For a local extension $F$ from step 4.1, the identity $e^{-1}\circ r\circ e\circ F=F$ holds near $q$; chain and Leibniz rules and the common jets from step 4.1 give equality of all jets of $\Phi$ and $F$ at $q\in A$. In particular $d\Phi_q=dF_q$ is invertible. Restrict to the open set $\Omega\subseteq\Omega_1$ where $d\Phi$ is invertible; it contains $A$, and $\Phi$ is a local diffeomorphism by [L7]. For each $p$, replace $W_p$ by $W_p\cap\Omega$. The original exponential formula remains a local diffeomorphism there and agrees with $\Phi$ on $W_p\cap A$. This proves (b), without asserting that the different exponential formulas agree on exterior overlaps. Countable Choice supplies [L5]-[L6], while Countable and Dependent Choice also accompany the boundary-structure supplier [L3].

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Local geodesics and exponential maps are smooth, convex normal neighborhoods exist, and exponential maps there have smooth inverses; timelike geodesic velocity stays timelike and has constant time orientation ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], [[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]], [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]).

steps.claim: (The interior past of a future boundary point.) Let $p\in C\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. If $x\in I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$, openness of $I^+(x)$ and the fact $p\in\partial U$ give $y\in U\cap I^+(x)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Concatenate a future timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $x$ with one from $x$ to $y$. Past convexity [L1] puts that curve, hence $x$, in $U$. Therefore $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)\subseteq U$. Choose a future timelike vector at $p$ and its local geodesic $\gamma$ with $\gamma(0)=p$; for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, its segment $\gamma([-\varepsilon,0))$ lies in $I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and hence in $U$. This establishes an actual affinely parametrized timelike geodesic, rather than replacing an arbitrary timelike curve by a geodesic.

(Local normal-coordinate extension.) Let $p'$ correspond to $p$. By [L3] $\varphi\circ\gamma\to p'$. Choose convex normal neighborhoods $V$ of $p$ and $V'$ of $p'$; shorten $\gamma$ so its entire segment and its image lie respectively in $V,V'$, and set $a=\gamma(-\varepsilon)$. By [L4] the image segment is an affinely parametrized geodesic. In the normal chart based at $\varphi(a)$ its inverse-exponential coordinates are its affine parameter times its initial velocity. Continuity at the limit $p'$ therefore gives $d\varphi_a(\exp_a^{-1}p)=\exp_{\varphi(a)}^{-1}p'$. Both vectors lie in the open normal-chart domains. Consequently, on a sufficiently small neighborhood $W$ of $p$, the formula $F_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a)}(d\varphi_a(\exp_a^{-1}q))$ is defined and is a diffeomorphism onto its open image. At $q=p$ the vector $\exp_a^{-1}p$ is future timelike; shrink $W\subseteq V\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ until every $\exp_a^{-1}q$ is future timelike as well. Its radial geodesic then joins $a$ to $q$ and stays in $V$. For $q\in W\cap U$, both endpoints lie in $U$, so causal convexity [L1] puts its entire radial segment in $U$. The connection-preserving property [L4] now gives $F_p(q)=\varphi(q)$. For past boundary points repeat with reversed time orientation and an interior base point $a\in I^+(p)\cap U$.

(Geodesic transfer.) In coordinates, the acceleration of $\Phi\circ\gamma$ is the image under $d\Phi$ of the acceleration of $\gamma$, with the difference term precisely the pullback-connection difference of step 6.1. For a geodesic whose entire image lies in $A$, both vanish at each parameter value, so its image is an affinely parametrized geodesic. The metric identity of step 6.1 preserves the zero squared velocity of a null geodesic. This proves (d).

facts.label: L4
facts.text: [L4] The development embedding $\varphi:U\to\varphi(U)$ is a diffeomorphism preserving metric, matter and time orientation. It preserves the metric-selected connection and affinely parametrized geodesics wherever their entire segments lie in $U$ ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]], [[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

steps.claim: (Local normal-coordinate extension.) Let $p'$ correspond to $p$. By [L3] $\varphi\circ\gamma\to p'$. (Openness and the boundary values.) If $q\in W\cap\partial U$, take points $q_n\in W\cap U$ tending to $q$ using a countable coordinate-neighborhood basis. Then $\varphi(q_n)=F_p(q_n)\to F_p(q)$. The limit cannot lie in $\varphi(U)$: continuity of $\varphi^{-1}$ there would force $q_n\to\varphi^{-1}(F_p(q))\in U$, contradicting Hausdorff uniqueness of the limit $q\in\partial U$. Thus $F_p(q)\in\partial\varphi(U)$, and the same sequence witnesses the neighborhood definition of correspondence. Hence $q\in C$ and $F_p(q)$ is its unique corresponding point. Each $p\in C$ has such a $W$, so $C$ is relatively open in $\partial U$. Define $f$ on $A:=U\cup C$ by $f|_U=\varphi$ and the unique corresponding values on $C$. (Homeomorphism on the closure side.) The map $f$ is injective on $U$; on $C$ it is injective by applying uniqueness of corresponding points to the reversed common subdevelopment, and its images of $U$ and $C$ are disjoint because they lie respectively in $\varphi(U)$ and its boundary. Write $C'$ for all corresponding boundary points on the primed side. Symmetry of the definition gives $f(A)=\varphi(U)\cup C'$. Apply the local construction of steps 1.1-2.1 to the reversed pair. Near every point of $C'$ it supplies a continuous local extension agreeing with $f^{-1}$ on its part of $\varphi(U)\cup C'$; on the open interior, the ordinary inverse $\varphi^{-1}$ supplies it. Hence $f^{-1}$ is continuous in the subspace topology, while $f$ is continuous as the restriction of $\Phi$. Thus $f:A\to f(A)$ is a homeomorphism. Thus any prescribed complete finite-jet Cauchy data of the fixed model are carried as well. This proves (e), in particular the full restart-hypersurface data identification.

(Curves through the sequence.) Assume $q\notin\Sigma$ and $q\notin I^-(\Sigma)$, so $q\in I^+(\Sigma)$ by [L1]; let $x_n\in K_q$. For each $n$ choose $\sigma_n\in\Sigma$ with $\sigma_n\le x_n$ and concatenate a causal curve from $\sigma_n$ to $x_n$ with one from $x_n$ to $q$, obtaining a future causal curve $\beta_n$ from $\sigma_n$ to $q$ whose image contains $x_n$, is contained in $J^+(\sigma_n)\cap J^-(q)$, and has finite $h$-arclength (a compact causal diamond) ([L1], [L3], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). Reparametrize $\beta_n$ by $h$-arclength from $q$ backwards: this gives a future causal curve $\alpha_n:[-L_n,0]\to M$ with $\alpha_n(0)=q$, $\alpha_n(-L_n)=\sigma_n$ and with $x_n=\alpha_n(-s_n)$ for the $h$-arclength $s_n\in[0,L_n]$ of the segment from $x_n$ to $q$.

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Global hyperbolicity of the development and closedness of the relations: $\Sigma$ Cauchy implies that $M$ is globally hyperbolic, hence strongly causal and causal, with closed causal relation; $J^-(q)$ and $J^+(\Sigma)$ are closed and $M=I^-(\Sigma)\sqcup\Sigma\sqcup I^+(\Sigma)$ ([[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]] clauses (a)-(b), [[lem-gr-globally-hyperbolic-causal-structure]] clause (a), [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]] clause (a)).

facts.label: L5
facts.text: [L5] Inextendible extension and compaction: a one-sided-inextendible causal curve is contained in an inextendible causal curve ([[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]] clause (d)); a closed causal segment lies on an inextendible causal curve ([[lem-gr-maximal-geodesics-and-extension]] clause (c)); a compact causal diamond is compact and a causal segment with endpoints in different components cannot be confined to one diamond ([[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]] clause (b)).

steps.claim: (The two easy cases.) If $q\in\Sigma$, and $x\in K_q$ with $x\ne q$: then $x\le q$ with $q\in\Sigma$; if $x\in I^+(\Sigma)$ then some $\sigma\in\Sigma$ satisfies $\sigma\ll x\le q$ with $\sigma\ne q$ or $\sigma=q$, and in either case $\sigma\le q$ relates two distinct points of $\Sigma$, contradicting acausality of Cauchy sets ([L1]); if $x\in\Sigma$ then $x\le q$ relates two points of $\Sigma$, so $x=q$, contradiction; the case $x\in I^-(\Sigma)$ is excluded by $J^+(\Sigma)\cap I^-(\Sigma)=\varnothing$ ([L1]). Hence $K_q=\{q\}$. If $q\in I^-(\Sigma)$, the same computation with $q$ in place of the generic point shows $K_q=\varnothing$.

steps.claim: (The bound.) Let $K$ be compact. By [L2] there is $\kappa(K)<\infty$ with $|(\nabla_Z h)(X,Y)|\le\kappa(K)|X|_h|Y|_h|Z|_h$ for all points of $K$ and all tangent vectors there. facts.label: L6
facts.text: [L6] In either development, $J^-(x)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ is compact; on the connected component traversed by a curve there is a smooth complete proper auxiliary metric $h$, and strong causality bounds the $h$-length of every compact causal subsegment contained in a fixed compact set. A geodesic with a compact tail, finite auxiliary length and a finite affine endpoint extends beyond that endpoint ([[lem-gr-compact-past-above-cauchy-set]], [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], [[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]], [[lem-gr-geodesic-extension-from-compact-length]] clause (b)). The length bound applies to past curves by reversing their parametrization.

steps.claim: (Follow only the initial connected component of corresponding points.) Let $J:=\{t\in[0,b]:\gamma(t)\in C\}$. It is relatively open and contains $0$ by [L5]. Define $s:=\sup\{t\in[0,b]:[0,t]\subseteq J\}$; relative openness at $0$ gives $s>0$, and every $0\le t<s$ belongs to $J$. On the interval $[0,s)$, the curve $f\circ\gamma=\Phi\circ\gamma$ is a past null affine geodesic by [L5]. Let $\eta$ be its unique maximal geodesic extension in $M'$, with the same parameter and initial data at $0$. Local uniqueness and connectedness give $\eta(t)=f(\gamma(t))$ for all $0\le t<s$; equivalently the interval solution itself is a restriction of the maximal solution. Each such value is a corresponding future boundary point, and hence belongs to $K':=J'^-(f(p_0))\cap J'^+(\Sigma')$, which is compact by [L6]. No connectedness of the entire open set $J$ has been assumed.

(Continuation of the image at the first possible exit.) The right endpoint $\beta'$ of the maximal domain of $\eta$ satisfies $\beta'\ge s$. If $\beta'=s$, its tail $\eta([0,s))$ lies in $K'$. On the component containing that curve choose the auxiliary complete proper metric $h'$ from [L6]; $K'$ intersected with this component is compact, since connected components of a manifold are closed. Strong causality gives a uniform length bound for every subsegment $\eta([0,t])$, $t<s$. Taking the supremum of these integrals gives finite $h'$-length of the entire tail. Since $s\le b<\infty$, the compact-length affine extension theorem [L6] extends $\eta$ beyond $s$, a contradiction. Thus $\beta'>s$, and $\eta(s)$ is an actual smooth geodesic value with $\eta(t)\to\eta(s)$ as $t\uparrow s$.

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Global hyperbolicity and closed relations: $\Sigma$ is Cauchy in $M$ and in $U$; $M$ and $U$ are globally hyperbolic, causal and strongly causal; $J^+(\Sigma)\cap J^-(\Sigma)=\Sigma$ and $M=I^-(\Sigma)\sqcup\Sigma\sqcup I^+(\Sigma)$ ([[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]], [[lem-gr-globally-hyperbolic-causal-structure]] clause (a), [[lem-gr-cauchy-set-topology-and-graph]] clause (a)).

steps.claim: (An initial boundary generator.) Choose $p_0\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$. Because $\Sigma\subseteq U$, the splitting in [L1] gives $p_0\in I^+(\Sigma)$. If the displayed exposed-point property already holds, take $p=p_0$. Otherwise choose a distinct $q_0\in J^-(p_0)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ and a causal curve joining them. Achronality [L2] and the null-versus-timelike alternative [L3] make this a null geodesic segment. Parametrize its maximal extension $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ in the past direction with $\gamma(0)=p_0$ and $\gamma(1)=q_0$. By [L4] it meets $\Sigma$ once, at a parameter $T>1$: a crossing at $T\le1$ would imply $q_0\in J^-(\Sigma)\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\Sigma$, impossible. All points $\gamma(t)$ for $0\le t<T$ lie in $I^+(\Sigma)$, because they are causally after $\gamma(T)\in\Sigma$, are not on $\Sigma$, and [L1] excludes the past side.

(No interior complement point below a future boundary.) Let $x\in\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and suppose $r\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with $r\le x$. Since $\Sigma\subseteq U$, one has $r\in I^+(\Sigma)$. Choose a sufficiently small past timelike perturbation $r_-\ll r$ inside the open set $\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Push-up gives $r_-\ll x$. The open neighborhood $I^+(r_-)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ of $x$ meets $U$, at $s$ say. Concatenate a timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $r_-$ with one from $r_-$ to $s$. Past convexity [L2] puts this entire curve in $U$, contradicting $r_-\notin U$. Thus no such $r$ exists. The perturbation is to the past, so the push-up direction is valid.

(Boundary-to-boundary causal segments stay on the boundary.) Let $y\le x$ be future boundary points and let $\eta$ be a future causal segment from $y$ to $x$. Every point $z$ of the segment lies in $I^+(\Sigma)$: some $\sigma\in\Sigma$ has $\sigma\ll y\le z$. If $z\in U$, concatenate a timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $y$ with the segment from $y$ to $z$; past convexity [L2] would give $y\in U$. If $z\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)$, step 1.2 with $z\le x$ gives a contradiction. Thus every point lies in $\partial U$. Achronality and [L3] further make every nonconstant such segment a null geodesic.

(The actual last boundary parameter before the Cauchy crossing.) Set $B:=\{t\in[0,T]:\gamma(t)\in\partial U\}$. It is closed in the compact interval $[0,T]$, contains $[0,1]$ by step 2.1, and misses a neighborhood of $T$ because $\gamma(T)\in\Sigma\subseteq U$. Whenever $t\in B$, step 2.1 applied to $\gamma(t)\le\gamma(0)$ puts $[0,t]$ in $B$. Therefore $B=[0,b]$ for its maximum $b$, with $1\le b<T<\beta$. In particular the whole segment $\gamma([0,b])$ is future boundary, and no parameter in $(b,T]$ is a boundary parameter. This establishes the interval property instead of assuming it for a closed preimage.

facts.text: [L1] Global hyperbolicity: $M$ is globally hyperbolic with closed causal relation, $M=I^-(\Sigma)\sqcup\Sigma\sqcup I^+(\Sigma)$ and $J^+(\Sigma)\cap J^-(\Sigma)=\Sigma$ ([[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]], [[lem-gr-globally-hyperbolic-causal-structure]] clause (a), [[lem-gr-corresponding-boundary-structure]] [L1] as used there).

steps.claim: (Setup.) Let $\gamma:[0,\varepsilon]\to M$ be a future timelike curve with $\gamma(0)=p$ (it exists since every point of a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold has a future timelike curve). If the conclusion failed for every $q=\gamma(t)$, there would be a sequence $t_j\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_j\to0$ and points $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(t_j))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$.

(The correctly directed complement exclusion.) Suppose $r\in\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ and $r\le p$. Since $\Sigma\subset U$, $r\notin\Sigma$ and hence $r\in I^+(\Sigma)$. Choose a short past timelike perturbation $r_-\ll r$ inside the open set $\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. Push-up gives $r_-\ll r\le p$, so $I^+(r_-)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is an open neighborhood of the boundary point $p$. It meets $U$ at $s$. A timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $r_-$ followed by one from $r_-$ to $s\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ contradicts past convexity [L4], because it passes through $r_-\notin U$. Thus there is no such $r$. This uses a past perturbation; no future perturbation below a null-related endpoint is inferred.

(Compactness and a limit.) Fix any $t_\ast\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_\ast\ge t_j$ for all $j$ (equivalently pass to the subsequence with $t_j\le\varepsilon$); then $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$ for all $j$. Since $U^c$ and $W^c$ are closed and $J^+(\Sigma)$ is closed [L1], the set $J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$ is closed in the compact set $J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ of [L2], hence compact; passing to a subsequence, $q_j\to q$ with $q\in J^-(\gamma(\varepsilon))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$.
($q\le p$.) Since $q_j\le\gamma(t_j)$ for every $j$, $q_j\to q$ and $\gamma(t_j)\to p$, closedness of the causal relation [L1] gives $q\le p$.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Limit curves and length upper semicontinuity: causal curves in a compact diamond with common initial point have uniformly convergent subsequences with causal limits, and Lorentzian length is upper semicontinuous under uniform convergence of causal curves ([[lem-gr-basic-limit-curve]], [[thm-gr-limit-curve-two-endpoints]], [[thm-gr-length-upper-semicontinuity]] clause (b)).

facts.label: L4
facts.text: [L4] Geodesics and maximizers: a causal curve realizes the time separation between its endpoints only if it has no timelike part and no corner and is a causal geodesic, as in the standard argument locating a maximizing curve ([[thm-gr-length-upper-semicontinuity]] clause (a) with [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]] clauses (b) and (d)); the speed $g(\gamma',\gamma')$ of a geodesic is constant ([[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]).

steps.claim: (Attainment and geodesy of maximizers.) Let $r\in J^-(q)\setminus\{q\}$ and, using Countable Choice, let $\alpha_n$ be causal curves from $r$ to $q$ with $L_g(\alpha_n)\to\tau_q(r)$. All images lie in the compact set $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$; reparametrizing by $h$-arclength from $r$ and applying [L2] gives a subsequence converging uniformly to a future causal curve $\gamma$ from $r$ to $q$, and upper semicontinuity of length [L2] gives $L_g(\gamma)\ge\limsup L_g(\alpha_n)=\tau_q(r)$, so $L_g(\gamma)=\tau_q(r)$. In every sufficiently small convex normal neighborhood, the local Lorentzian normal-maximum theorem [L3] bounds the length of a subarc by that of its radial causal geodesic, with equality only along that geodesic up to increasing reparametrization. If any subarc failed this equality condition, finite replacement would strictly increase the total length, contradicting maximality. Thus all local subarcs have geodesic images; on overlaps they have the same tangent ray and geodesic uniqueness joins them into a single causal geodesic up to monotone reparametrization, and its image lies in $J^+(r)\cap J^-(q)$.

(Upper semicontinuity on compact sets.) Let $r_n\to r$ in a compact $K$. If $\limsup\tau_q(r_n)=0$, upper semicontinuity is immediate from nonnegativity. Otherwise take a subsequence approaching that positive limsup; discard zero-separation terms, so every remaining $r_n\ne q$ is causally related to $q$. Choose, by Countable Choice, $\alpha_n$ be causal curves from $r_n$ to $q$ with $L_g(\alpha_n)\ge\tau_q(r_n)-1/n$. Passing to the compact diamond $J^+(K')\cap J^-(q)$ for a compact $K'$ containing the $r_n$ ([L1]), [L2] gives a subsequence of the $\alpha_n$, reparametrized by $h$-arclength, converging uniformly to a causal curve from $r$ to $q$, and $\limsup_n\tau_q(r_n)\le\limsup_nL_g(\alpha_n)\le L_g(\gamma)\le\tau_q(r)$ by upper semicontinuity [L2] and step 2.1. If $r\in I^-(q)$ then a maximizer $\gamma_r$ from $r$ to $q$ exists (step 2.1); since $I^-(q)$ is open, for $n$ large the inner segment of $\gamma_r$ can be joined to $r_n$ by a short timelike segment inside $I^-(q)$, giving $\liminf_n\tau_q(r_n)\ge\tau_q(r)$ by letting the inner cut shrink; combined with the upper bound this gives continuity at $r$.

If $r\notin J^-(q)$ no such curve exists and $\tau_q(r)=0$; if $r=q$ causality excludes a nonconstant return curve and the stipulated zero-separation convention gives $\tau_q(q)=0$; and $\tau_q(r)>0$ iff there is a future timelike curve from $r$ to $q$, i.e. $r\in I^-(q)$.

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] The developments are globally hyperbolic. Time separation is finite and upper semicontinuous on compact sets, with its positive set $I^-(q)$ and its smooth radial formula on the causally convex $W\subset C$; $J^+(\Sigma)$ is closed and $J^-(q)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ is compact ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]], [[lem-gr-compact-past-above-cauchy-set]], [[lem-gr-globally-hyperbolic-causal-structure]]).

steps.claim: (Maximum and its boundary location.) The compact set $K$ is nonempty because it contains $p$; $\tau_q$ is finite and upper semicontinuous on $K$, so its maximum is attained and $\tau_0\ge\tau_q(p)>0$ by [L1]. A maximizer $r$ belongs to $I^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$, hence to $W$ by the assumed containment, and to $I^+(\Sigma)$ since $r\notin\Sigma\subset U$. If $r$ were interior to $U^c$, the timelike radial geodesic from $r$ to $q$ could be continued a little to the past within $W\cap\operatorname{int}(U^c)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ by [L2]. Its extended positive proper length exceeds $\tau_0$, contradicting maximality on $K$. Thus every maximizer lies in $W\cap\partial U\subset C_{\mathrm{corr}}$. If $x\in W$ has $\tau_q(x)>\tau_0$ and is outside $U$, then $x\in K$ because $W\subset I^+(\Sigma)$, a contradiction. The same boundary-location argument applies to each $x\in W\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ with $\tau_q(x)=\tau_0$. This proves (a).

(The complete level surface and compact ambient closure.) On $W\cap I^-(q)$ define $R(x)=\sqrt{-g_q(\xi(x),\xi(x))}$ with $\xi=\exp_q^{-1}x$; by [L1], $R=	au_q$ there. The Gauss differential [L2] gives $
abla R=-P(q,x)/R$, so $g(
abla R,
abla R)=-1$ and $
abla R$ is future-directed; its negative $X$ is unit past-directed. The level $	au_q=	au_0>0$ is therefore a smooth spacelike hypersurface in $W$. Its connected components are open and closed in this regular level, so the specified component $S$ is embedded without boundary and closed relative to $W$. It contains the chosen boundary maximizer, and every point of $S\setminus U$ is a boundary maximizer by step 1.1. Hence (b) holds. Let $A=\overline S^{\,M}\subset\overline W$; this is compact, although $S$ itself need not be compact. In the normal chart of $C$, every limit point of $S$ still has past timelike inverse vector of norm squared $-	au_0^2$. Thus $R$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $A$ in $C$, and $A$ lies in its regular level $R=	au_0$.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] Normal geometry gives the smooth inverse exponential on $C$, radial geodesics and the Gauss differential $d(g_q(\exp_q^{-1}x,\exp_q^{-1}x))=2g(P(q,x),\cdot)$, with constant radial geodesic speed ([[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]], [[lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism]], [[lem-gr-position-vector-differential]], [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]], [[thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone]]). Smooth geodesic/flow existence, uniqueness and parameter dependence are [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], [[thm-fundamental-theorem-on-flows]] and [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]; an injective transverse flowout is [[thm-flowout-theorem]].

(Quantitative normal flow over the ambient closure.) Extend $X=-\nabla R$ to its smooth domain near $A$. The radial formula shows directly that its flow is $F(s,t)=\exp_q((1+t/\tau_0)\xi(s))$ while defined, so $R(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$ and its lines are unit affinely parametrized past timelike geodesics by [L2]. Compactness of $A$ and openness of the smooth flow domain give $a>0$, an open neighbourhood $B$ of $A$ in the extended level, and a compact ambient set containing every $F(s,t)$ for $s\in B$, $|t|\le a$ after shrinking $B,a$. Smoothness of $dF$ and the positive metric on the extended level permit a further uniform shrinking with $\tfrac12q_0\le q_t\le2q_0$, where $q_t(V,V)=g(dF_tV,dF_tV)$ for $V$ tangent to that level. To see uniformity, the $h$-unit tangent bundle over compact $A$ is compact, $q_0$ has a positive minimum there and $q_t-q_0$ tends uniformly to zero; the bounds then persist near $A$. Likewise choose constants $c,C>0$ with $q_0\ge ch|_{TS}$ and $|X|_h\le C$ throughout this compact flow range. The flow speed gives $d_h(F(s,t),s)\le C|t|$. These are bounds on a compact extended level neighbourhood, not an assumption that $S$ is compact.

(Injectivity, the open tube and its metric.) Restrict the smooth flow to $\mathcal D_\delta=\{(s,t):s\in S,\ |t|<\delta(s)\}$. It is defined by step 4.1, and $\tau_q(F(s,t))=\tau_0+t$ because its image lies in $W$. If $F(s,t)=F(s',t')$, this identity gives $t=t'$ and flow uniqueness gives $s=s'$. Its differential is invertible at the zero section because $X$ is transverse to $S$, and everywhere by the flow group law; hence [L2] makes it a diffeomorphism onto an open $N\subset O$. Vectors $dF_tV$ are tangent to the $R$-level and orthogonal to $X$, so $F^*g=-dt^2+q_t$. All construction claims in (c), including its quantitative inequalities, now hold.

(Noncompact surface ends and the Cauchy conclusion.) If instead $e\in A\setminus S$, relative closedness gives $e\in\partial W$. Step 4.1 gives $\delta(s)\to0$, so the tube inequality forces $H=0$ and the smooth extended flow gives $\gamma\to e$. The point $e\in\overline W\subset C\subset I^+(\Sigma)$ has past timelike inverse exponential of radial norm $\tau_0$, so $e\in I^-(q)$ by [L2]. If $e\notin U$, the assumed containment $J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subset W$ would give $e\in W$, contradicting $e\in\partial W$. Therefore $e\in U$, again an endpoint in $U\cup N$. With step 7.1 this proves there is no $U$-avoiding inextendible curve. For any inextendible curve meeting $U$, [L5] makes each maximal $U$-portion inextendible in $U$, so it meets $\Sigma$ once. If two parameter visits to $\Sigma$ existed, [L3]'s causal convexity puts the intervening segment in $U$, making both visits belong to the same maximal $U$-portion, a contradiction. This proves (c)2 for the entire noncompact surface.

(The map comparison and admissible thinner tubes.) For the conditional local isometry $\Theta$ of (c)3, its differential agrees with $d\Phi$ on $TS$ and, since both are future isometries at $S$, on the future unit normal by [L3], [L6]. They therefore agree on $X$, the past unit normal. The punctured radial segment of step 6.2 lies in $U$, so $\varphi$ maps it to an affinely parametrized geodesic by [L6], with limiting value and velocity at the base supplied by its smooth extension $\Phi$. The $\Theta$-image is a geodesic with the identical base value and velocity. Geodesic uniqueness [L2] gives $\Theta(y)=\varphi(y)$. Finally any smaller smooth positive width with the derivative bound in (c)4 inherits the flow domain, metric comparisons, speed bounds and vanishing at $A\setminus S$. The same proof uses $|d\widetilde\delta(s')|\le\tfrac14|t'|$ in step 7.1, still giving strict signed-face monotonicity; all other steps are unchanged. Step 4.1 already allows any prescribed open $O$ and ceiling $b$. Thus (c)3-4 and all conclusions hold.

abla R=-P(q,x)/R$, so $g(
abla R,

abla R=-P(q,x)/R$, so $g(
abla R,
abla R)=-1$ and $
abla R$ is future-directed; its negative $X$ is unit past-directed. The level $	au_q=	au_0>0$ is therefore a smooth spacelike hypersurface in $W$. It crosses $t=0$ at most once. At either time end, tail $q_0$-length tends to zero; $q_0\ge ch$ from step 3.1 makes $s(\lambda)$ Cauchy in $d_h$, with a unique limit in compact $A$. Maximal portions of an inextendible curve in an open subset are inextendible there ([[lem-gr-portion-inextendibility]]). The common subdevelopment has $\Sigma$ Cauchy ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]).

steps.claim: (Causal graphs and finite base length.) For a future causal curve $\gamma(\lambda)=F(s(\lambda),t(\lambda))$ in $N$, [L5] and step 5.1 give $q_t(s',s')\le(t')^2$ almost everywhere. Since $\nabla R$ is future timelike, $t'=dR(\gamma')<0$ almost everywhere, and the fundamental theorem makes $t$ strictly decreasing. The lower comparison bound gives $|s'|_{q_0}\le\sqrt2|t'|$ and hence the total $q_0$-length is at most $\sqrt2\operatorname{var}(t)\le2\sqrt2\sup_S\delta<\infty$. Thus the image is a graph in the time coordinate; integrated length on subintervals gives a locally Lipschitz graph in any base chart, without assuming that the inverse of the original time parametrization is a $C^1$ map. It crosses $t=0$ at most once. At either time end, tail $q_0$-length tends to zero; $q_0\ge ch$ from step 3.1 makes $s(\lambda)$ Cauchy in $d_h$, with a unique limit in compact $A$. Past curves are handled by reversal. This proves (c)1 and supplies the endpoint control used below.

(Exact radial interior.) Let $y=F(s,t_y)\in N\cap U$. For $t_y>0$, all radial points with $0<u\le t_y$ lie in $U$ by step 1.1 because their time separation exceeds $\tau_0$; the base may lie on $\partial U$ and is excluded from this assertion. For $t_y<0$, $s$ is to the chronological past of $y$. Concatenate a timelike curve from $\Sigma$ to $s$ (since $s\in W\subset I^+(\Sigma)$) with the radial segment from $s$ to $y$. Its endpoint is $y\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$, so [L3]'s past-convexity clause puts the whole concatenation, including $s$ and the radial segment, in $U$. If $t_y=0$, $s=y\in U$ directly. If $s\in U$ and $t_y>0$, causal convexity with endpoints $y,s\in U$ also puts the inclusive segment in $U$. This proves precisely the radial assertions in (c)3.

(Past endpoint of a hypothetical avoiding curve.) Suppose a future causal curve $\gamma$ inextendible in $U\cup N$ avoids $U$. Then it lies in $N$ and has $t\le0$ by step 1.1; equality may occur and is not excluded without proof. At its past end the decreasing time has supremum limit $H\le0$, and step 6.1 gives $s\to e\in A$. If $e\in S$, continuity and the tube inequalities imply $H\ge-\delta(e)$. If $H>-\delta(e)$, then also $H<\delta(e)$ since $\delta(e)>0$, so the smooth extended flow gives endpoint $F(e,H)\in N$, contradicting inextendibility. The only remaining possibility is $H=-\delta(e)$. Along the curve set $r=t+\delta(s)>0$. The actual derivative bound yields $r'=t'+d\delta(s')\le-(1-1/8)|t'|$, hence for any two ordered parameter values $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$, $r(\lambda_1)-r(\lambda_2)\ge(7/8)(t(\lambda_1)-t(\lambda_2))>0$. A past-end limit $r\to H+\delta(e)=0$ is impossible because it is at least the positive value of $r$ at each fixed later parameter. This excludes the signed lower face with the correct direction of monotonicity; no analysis of a second endpoint is needed.

(Noncompact surface ends and the Cauchy conclusion.) If instead $e\in A\setminus S$, relative closedness gives $e\in\partial W$. Step 4.1 gives $\delta(s)\to0$, so the tube inequality forces $H=0$ and the smooth extended flow gives $\gamma\to e$. The point $e\in\overline W\subset C\subset I^+(\Sigma)$ has past timelike inverse exponential of radial norm $\tau_0$, so $e\in I^-(q)$ by [L2]. If $e\notin U$, the assumed containment $J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subset W$ would give $e\in W$, contradicting $e\in\partial W$. Therefore $e\in U$, again an endpoint in $U\cup N$. With step 7.1 this proves there is no $U$-avoiding inextendible curve. For any inextendible curve meeting $U$, [L5] makes each maximal $U$-portion inextendible in $U$, so it meets $\Sigma$ once. If two parameter visits to $\Sigma$ existed, [L3]'s causal convexity puts the intervening segment in $U$, making both visits belong to the same maximal $U$-portion, a contradiction. This proves (c)2 for the entire noncompact surface.

facts.label: L6
facts.text: [L6] Local isometries preserve the Levi-Civita connection and affinely parametrized geodesics; their differentials take the future unit normal of a spacelike hypersurface to the future unit normal of its image ([[lem-gr-isometric-immersion-rigidity]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]).

steps.claim: (The map comparison and admissible thinner tubes.) For the conditional local isometry $\Theta$ of (c)3, its differential agrees with $d\Phi$ on $TS$ and, since both are future isometries at $S$, on the future unit normal by [L3], [L6]. They therefore agree on $X$, the past unit normal. The punctured radial segment of step 6.2 lies in $U$, so $\varphi$ maps it to an affinely parametrized geodesic by [L6], with limiting value and velocity at the base supplied by its smooth extension $\Phi$. The $\Theta$-image is a geodesic with the identical base value and velocity. Geodesic uniqueness [L2] gives $\Theta(y)=\varphi(y)$. Finally any smaller smooth positive width with the derivative bound in (c)4 inherits the flow domain, metric comparisons, speed bounds and vanishing at $A\setminus S$. The same proof uses $|d\widetilde\delta(s')|\le\tfrac14|t'|$ in step 7.1, still giving strict signed-face monotonicity; all other steps are unchanged. Step 4.1 already allows any prescribed open $O$ and ceiling $b$. Thus (c)3-4 and all conclusions hold.

facts.label: L2
facts.text: [L2] A complete auxiliary Riemannian metric with compact closed bounded balls exists, and sequences of its arclength-parametrized one-sided inextendible causal curves whose starting points converge have inextendible causal subsequential limits uniformly on compact parameter intervals ([[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], [[lem-gr-basic-limit-curve]]). The dual limit statement holds for past curves.

steps.claim: We explain the arclength use in [L2]. For an avoiding one-sided causal curve, restrict to the half ending at the prescribed point. Its $h$-speed is locally integrable and positive almost everywhere, so its accumulated $h$-length is continuous strictly increasing. The inverse parameter gives a curve which is $1$-Lipschitz for $d_h$, because distance is at most original subcurve length; hence it is locally Lipschitz in charts. To verify the tangent and the arclength identity without assuming absolute continuity of the inverse parameter, let $\lambda(t)$ denote accumulated length. At almost every original parameter, both the chart curve and $\lambda$ are differentiable and $\lambda'(t)=\sqrt{h(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))}>0$. Their exceptional set has measure zero. An absolutely continuous real function sends a measure-zero set to a measure-zero set: cover that set by intervals of arbitrarily small total length and apply the defining AC modulus to bound the total lengths of their image intervals. Thus its image under $\lambda$ is null, locally and hence on a countable exhaustion. At each remaining new parameter $u=\lambda(t)$, the inverse difference quotient is $1/\lambda'(t)$, and the chain difference quotient of the reparametrized chart curve is $\gamma'(t)/\lambda'(t)$. It is nonzero future causal and has $h$-norm one. This proves both admissibility and $h$-arclength parametrization. If the available one-sided length were finite, the $1$-Lipschitz curve would be Cauchy at that end and completeness would give a point limit, contrary to inextendibility. Thus these reparametrizations have full half-line domains, as required by [L2]. This argument changes parameters and never asserts an extension preserving an arbitrary original parameter.

Let $p\in D^+(S)\setminus S$. If $p$ were not interior to $D^+(S)$, choose $p_k\notin D^+(S)$ converging to $p$ and past-inextendible curves ending at $p_k$ and avoiding $S$. Step 1.2 and [L2] give a past-inextendible causal limit $\alpha:(-\infty,0]\to W$ with $\alpha(0)=p$. It meets $S$ at a negative parameter, by $p\in D^+(S)$ and $p\notin S$. By step 3.1 a short compact segment around that meeting crosses the local graph strictly. Uniform convergence on that segment forces the avoiding approximants to meet $S$, contradiction. Therefore $D^+(S)\setminus S$ is open; time reversal gives the dual result.

Let $s\in S$. If $s$ were not interior to $D(S)$, take $p_k\notin D(S)$ converging to $s$. At each $p_k$ choose a past-inextendible avoiding half and a future-inextendible avoiding half, concatenate them, and use step 1.2 to parametrize the two halves by signed arclength with $p_k$ at zero. Apply [L2] first to their past halves and then to the future halves of that subsequence. The two limits join at $s$ to an inextendible causal curve, and the common subsequence converges uniformly on each compact interval of the joined domain. Its short crossing segment through $s$ from step 3.1 forces the avoiding curves to meet $S$, contradiction. Thus $S\subset\operatorname{Int}D(S)$; together with step 4.2 and step 4.1 this proves (a).

facts.label: L1
facts.text: [L1] Temporal coordinate balls exist with a finite upper causal-speed bound, future timelike vertical fibers, and a narrower constant cone whose timelike straight segments are $g$-timelike ([[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]]). Chronology is open and satisfies push-up in both directions ([[lem-gr-chronology-openness]], [[lem-gr-push-up-rule]]).

steps.claim: Fix $s\in S$. There is no timelike loop through $s$: if $s\ll s$, openness gives $s\ll s'$ for all $s'\in S$ sufficiently near $s$, and the topological hypersurface has points $s'\ne s$ arbitrarily near $s$, contrary to acausality. Thus no two points of $S$, equal or distinct, are chronologically related. In particular $I^+(S)$ and $I^-(S)$ are disjoint by push-up.

Edgelessness supplies an open neighborhood $O$ of $s$ in which every timelike curve from $I^-_O(s)$ to $I^+_O(s)$ meets $S$. Take a temporal coordinate box $B=(-a,a)\times B_\rho$ with closure in $O$, centered at $s$. First choose $a>0$ small, and then $\rho>0$ small enough that all points $(-a,z)$ and $(a,z)$ belong respectively to $I^-_O(s)$ and $I^+_O(s)$; the narrower constant cone of [L1] ensures this. Every vertical segment between these endpoints therefore meets $S$, and has only one meeting by step 1.1. Write it $(f(z),z)$. The same narrower cone implies $|f(z)-f(z')|\le C|z-z'|$: otherwise the two graph points are joined by a timelike straight segment in $O$, contrary to step 1.1. Consequently $S\cap B$ is exactly a continuous Lipschitz graph; the sign of $t-f(z)$ separates the box into two open sides. A point above the graph belongs to $I^+(S)$ by its vertical segment; a point below belongs to $I^-(S)$.

A future causal segment starting at $s$ and remaining in this box cannot have an endpoint $q$ below the graph: the vertical segment from $q$ to the graph point $r$ gives $s\le q\ll r$, so $s\ll r$, excluded by step 1.1. If $q\in S$ and $q\ne s$, acausality excludes it. If $q=s$ but the segment is nondegenerate, choose an intermediate point $q'$ different from $s$ sufficiently near its start; it cannot lie below the graph or on $S$, so lies above it. Its vertical predecessor $r'\in S$ satisfies $r'\ll q'\le s$, again excluded by step 1.1. The same argument applies even if the rest of the loop leaves the box. Thus no nondegenerate causal loop passes through $S$, no causal curve meets $S$ twice, and every sufficiently short future segment from $S$ lies strictly above its local graph. Reversing time puts short past segments strictly below. Every causal curve through $s$ therefore crosses its local graph, and uniform approximations of a sufficiently short compact crossing segment also meet that graph by continuity of $t-f(z)$ and the intermediate value theorem.

If $q\in J^+(S)\setminus S$, take a causal curve $s\to q$ and a point $r$ on a sufficiently short initial segment. Step 3.1 puts $r$ above the graph. Its vertical predecessor $u\in S$ gives $u\ll r\le q$, hence $q\in I^+(S)$. Dually $J^-(S)\setminus S\subset I^-(S)$. For $p\in D^+(S)\setminus S$, the past half of the maximal timelike geodesic through $p$ is past-inextendible by [L3], and hence meets $S$; its timelike segment from that meeting to $p$ puts $p\in I^+(S)$. The dual argument proves the past-side inclusion. Also $S\subset D^+(S)\cap D^-(S)$ immediately.

For a segment $p\to q$ in the remaining mixed case $p\in D^-(S)$, $q\in D^+(S)$, an intermediate $r\notin D(S)$ has both past- and future-inextendible avoiding halves. Concatenating the past half with $r\to q$ forces a meeting of $S$ strictly after $r$, and concatenating $p\to r$ with the future half forces a meeting strictly before $r$. This contradicts step 3.1. The opposite mixed case $p\in D^+(S)$, $q\in D^-(S)$ is impossible for a nondegenerate segment: step 4.1 yields $p\in S\cup I^+(S)$, $q\in S\cup I^-(S)$; if either endpoint is outside $S$, push-up gives a chronological relation between points of $S$, excluded by step 1.1, and if both are in $S$, step 3.1 excludes the segment. Along with step 5.2 this proves (b).

facts.label: L3
facts.text: [L3] Local complete-data geometric uniqueness is required for the fixed admissible coupled model at the actual restart data, as specified in [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]. Use [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] when its full initialization, hyperbolicity, compatibility recovery and stress-conservation hypotheses hold on this spacelike surface. Scalar and strict-fluid instances are [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]], [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]]. Geodesic nonnegative tilted dust instead uses [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] with its independent common-flow/frame reduction, including its separately prescribed velocity on zero density. Complete data, including all required matter jets, agree by [L2]; the comparison isometry matches every matter field. An arbitrary conserved stress is not a fixed-model uniqueness premise.

steps.claim: (Local uniqueness on the whole restart surface.) The complete data of $S$ realized in $M$ and in $M'$ via $\Phi|_S$ agree by [L2]. Apply [L4] to obtain intrinsic Cauchy neighborhoods of each surface, carrying the restricted metric and full matter solution. The applicable fixed-model theorem [L3] gives an open neighborhood $O$ of the whole $S$ in the source and a future isometry $\Theta:O\to M'$ matching all matter fields, with $\Theta|_S=\Phi|_S$. Replace $O$ by $O\cap N$. This construction uses the actual branch uniqueness theorem and its admissibility at the realized restart data.
